clue.text: It can raise a smile — even when blue?

definitions.text: It can raise a smile — even when blue?

blocks.note: surface reading: a joke or a funny sight that makes someone grin, even a risqué blue one
setter's reading: the word photographers ask you to say, and also a food that can come in blue-veined varieties like Stilton

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a joke can still get a laugh even when it is smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue here first suggests a rude joke, but the thing meant is also a dairy product with a famous blue-veined kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers tell sitters to say it so their mouths form a grin, and Stilton or Roquefort are blue varieties.

clue.text: City provides stylish area with work

blocks.note: fashionable and elegant
A is the abbreviation for area
to go is to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: A town offers fashionable neighbourhoods along with jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Illinois metropolis on Lake Michigan is the third-largest urban centre in the United States.

clue.text: Foremost of experts consulted on lingering infection source

definitions.text: Foremost of experts consulted on lingering infection source

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Leading specialists are called in about where a persistent illness comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: what experts would be asked about is the bacterium behind an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Escherichia coli is a gut bacterium whose harmful strains cause food poisoning outbreaks.

clue.text: Climbing rodents fed with form of protein shake

indicators.note: being fed with something means taking it inside, so one word goes into the other
in a down clue climbing means going upward, so the combined letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: rats are rodents
an egg is a common source of protein

explanation.surface: Rats scrambling upward after being given a protein milkshake.
explanation.walkthrough: Shake looks like a drink to go with the protein, but it is the verb; in a down clue the whole combination is read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter or reel unsteadily, as a person walking while dizzy would wobble.

clue.text: Get that woman sounding like an emperor

indicators.note: the phrase asks us to say the words before it out loud and listen to what they resemble

blocks.note: to get is to seize, and that woman is her

explanation.surface: Someone urges catching a woman whose voice or manner is as grand as royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius's family name became the title taken by Roman rulers, so it serves as a word for an imperial monarch.

clue.text: Essential fact jurors missed from one side to the other

definitions.text: from one side to the other

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so the central letters of each word are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters
the two central letters
the two central letters

explanation.surface: A jury overlooked a crucial piece of evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means traversing something, from one edge or bank to the opposite one.

clue.text: Prove a sun exploded like this

definitions.text: Prove a sun exploded like this

indicators.note: an explosion scatters the pieces, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An astronomer's challenge to demonstrate that a star blew up in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a star's explosion is exactly what the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A star that blows itself apart in a sudden, enormously bright stellar explosion is given this astronomical name.

clue.text: Truth illuminated in rough year

indicators.note: rough means unpolished or approximate, so the next word's letters are jumbled
in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, before rearranging
lit means lit up

explanation.surface: The facts came to light during a difficult twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of things as they actually exist, rather than as imagined, is what truth amounts to.

clue.text: Unimpressive report of minor earthquake

blocks.note: first meaning: an idiom for mediocre or not very good
second meaning taken literally: a seismic event without strong tremors

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning reads the idiom literally, as a news line saying the tremors were mild.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal idiom describes something mediocre or not much good, and literally says the tremors were small.

clue.text: Writer providing life story about queen

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: short for biography
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An author produces a biography of a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer looks like an author, but it means a pen; R goes inside BIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint pen is commonly called by this brand name in Britain, and a pen is something you write with.

clue.text: Happy coral is damaged? That may not be true

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters before it get rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether cheerful reef life has been harmed, followed by a doubt that the story is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories of doubtful authenticity, widely told but probably invented, are described with this adjective.

clue.text: In need of time out when on the decline

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter leaves the longer word

blocks.note: lacking or needing something
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone who needs a break when their fortunes are sinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the T out of WANTING to leave WANING.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of the moon or of influence, it means shrinking or fading, so it describes something going down.

clue.text: Check pressure again

blocks.note: the prefix meaning again
strain is stress or pressure

explanation.surface: An instruction to measure the force once more, like testing tyres.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the reverse of clue order: RE goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it, the verb meaning to keep under control.

clue.text: Fantastic shot taker has very successful run

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the following letters are rearranged into an unrecognisable form

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sporting marksman who is on a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: Fantastic looks like praise for the shooter, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler or player enjoying a sequence of consecutive wins is said to be on this kind of streak.

clue.text: Demonstrate test that guarantees conviction

blocks.note: to show is to demonstrate
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Running an experiment to prove a firmly held belief.
explanation.walkthrough: Conviction reads as firm belief, but it is the court's guilty verdict; test serves in both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged court proceeding, typical of authoritarian regimes, where the guilty verdict is decided in advance for propaganda.

clue.text: Sly return of axes

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the short word after it is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
the x and y axes of a graph

explanation.surface: A crafty comeback of hatchets, as though a weapon were thrown back.
explanation.walkthrough: Return of looks like a phrase, but the return applies to the word 'of' itself; axes are the graph's x and y, not hatchets.
explanation.definitionFit: Cunning like the proverbial fox, the adjective describes someone crafty and wily.

clue.text: Explode without full force? That's a mistake

indicators.note: without the full amount means something is dropped, so one letter of the doubled pair goes

blocks.note: to explode, as a bomb does
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A bomb that fizzles rather than blowing up properly is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: GO OFF loses one of its two Fs to leave GOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal noun for a silly error or blunder, also usable as a verb for messing up.

clue.text: Lined out to break horse, lacking cojones!

indicators.note: out means put out of place, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged
breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, before rearranging
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: Riders queue up to tame a stallion, which turns out to be castrated.
explanation.walkthrough: Break suggests taming a horse; here it means split GG open. Horse does double duty in wordplay and definition; cojones is Spanish slang for testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated male horse is the stable term for a stallion that has been neutered.

clue.text: Criminal stole a car — it gets things moving

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or crooked, so the letters that follow are bent out of their order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A joyrider steals a vehicle and gets the investigation going.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: the moving staircase carries people and things up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase in shops and stations carries people between floors, so it literally sets loads in motion.

clue.text: A group performing 'Surrender'

blocks.note: taken as written
a musical group
on stage, as performers are

explanation.surface: A pop group playing a song titled Surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make Surrender look like a song title; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or relinquish something completely, such as a ship or a claim, is to yield it.

clue.text: Rode off, embarrassed to get booked

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of the word before it are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written, before rearranging
red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: A rider leaves in a fluster after being cautioned by the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: Booked suggests a footballer being cautioned; here it means reserved in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Requesting goods or a table in advance means they have been reserved, so ordered and booked are synonyms.

clue.text: One can be taken in with room to spare

definitions.text: One can be taken in with room to spare

blocks.clueFragment: One can be taken in with room to spare
blocks.note: surface reading: something easily absorbed or fooled with plenty of margin left
setter's reading: a person given accommodation, who pays to occupy a householder's spare bedroom

explanation.surface: Someone is easily deceived, with capacity left over.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken in sounds like deceived and room to spare like a wide margin; both are literal here, a person housed in a spare room.
explanation.definitionFit: A paying tenant who rents a room in someone else's home, usually a householder's unused bedroom.

clue.text: God is into prayer a lot

indicators.note: one thing being into another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: an earnest request or appeal
the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A believer who prays frequently and devoutly.
explanation.walkthrough: God here is the Norse thunder god rather than a generic deity, and 'a lot' is the definition, not a filler phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means an excess or great abundance, a large quantity of something.

clue.text: Schedule time with new father

blocks.note: an age is a period of time
N is the abbreviation for new
an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: Planning a timetable that fits around a recent dad's needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be discussed or done at a meeting is a kind of plan or programme.

clue.text: Lacking information, one or the other might knock you out

definitions.note: a noun defined by what it does

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the abbreviation that follows is removed

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for information, as on tourist signs
either means one or the other of two

explanation.surface: Without knowledge, any of the options could flatten you.
explanation.walkthrough: Knock you out sounds like a punch, but it means make you unconscious. Remove I from EITHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Diethyl ether was once a widely used general anaesthetic, inhaled to render patients unconscious.

clue.text: Schrödinger's cat, perhaps, reduced to a zombie?

blocks.note: first meaning: the thought-experiment cat that is both alive and deceased at once
second meaning: the undead of horror films

explanation.surface: A joke that the famous quantum cat ends up as one of the undead.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning takes the phrase literally, alive and not alive at once; the second is the horror-film term for corpses that walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror films call walking corpses by this phrase, and the paradoxical quantum cat is simultaneously breathing and lifeless.

clue.text: Home rule decentralised in this place

indicators.note: with the centres taken away, only the outside letters of each word remain

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A political slogan about devolved self-government being in force locally.
explanation.walkthrough: Home rule and decentralised suggest devolution politics, but the instruction is to strip the middles from both words.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb points to the speaker's present location, meaning at or in this spot.

clue.text: Convict returns with mineral — and plenty of it

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective placed after a noun, meaning in abundance

indicators.note: something that returns goes back, so the word for convict is read backwards

blocks.note: an old lag is British slang for a long-serving prisoner
rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A released prisoner comes back with a hoard of precious rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed after a noun, as in prizes galore, the word means in great quantity or abundance.

clue.text: Seasoned judge leaving hurt

indicators.note: the judge leaving means that letter departs from the word that follows

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
wounded or harmed

explanation.surface: An experienced magistrate quits the bench after being wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: Seasoned suggests experience or flavouring; here it means hardened. Remove J from INJURED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hardened by long exposure to hardship has become accustomed to it, as a seasoned veteran is.
